we introduce a new training method for IDMs, that uses an autoencoder and a discriminator to guide learning of a latent representation that encodes information that is shared between equivalent experiences.
we design a training process for Inverse Dynamics Models that guides the learning process of latent representations to capture the information shared between experiences.
learning a representation of shared information between equivalent experiences enables the learning of goal-conditioned inverse dynamics models for locomotion tasks.

learning latent representations that encode the information shared between different experiences.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose a novel approach for learning IDMs, and demonstrate that it can be successfully applied to high-dimensional locomotion tasks.
our approach is able to learn a goal-conditioned IDM that can be applied to a wide range of tasks, without requiring task-specific training.
we present a method that learns to perform goal-directed locomotion in high dimensional environments, and show that the key lies in learning the latent information shared by equivalent experiences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to learn latent representations that can be used to generalize IDMs to new environments, and we demonstrate how to use this to achieve goal-conditioned locomotion in complex environments.

we show that the key for IDMs lies in the ability to learn latent representations for generalizing between equivalent experiences, and that our approach is a simple yet effective method to achieve this.
we are the first to learn IDMs for locomotion tasks in the continuous action space.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of IDMs can be improved by learning a latent representation that generalizes over experiences.
by learning latent representations that capture shared information across equivalent experiences, we can achieve high performance on challenging robot locomotion tasks.
by learning to encode shared information, we are able to learn more generalizable IDMs that can be applied to unseen goals and environments.
